summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, and chronic pain from prior trauma, was admitted after returning to the emergency department with severe shortness of breath and alcohol intoxication. He had left AMA the prior day but returned due to worsening respiratory symptoms. Imaging showed recurrent right middle lobe collapse and findings consistent with acute on chronic aspiration, but no malignancy. He was treated for a COPD exacerbation with oral steroids and antibiotics, and for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and supportive vitamins. His sodium normalized with oral hydration, and he was weaned off oxygen. Despite clinical improvement, he elected to leave against medical advice on hospital day two, declining discharge medications and follow-up instructions due to dissatisfaction with pain management. He was warned of the risks of untreated withdrawal and respiratory decline.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
